item.title: Self-extubation in critically ill patients: new predictors identified in a multicenter retrospective study
item.description: Introduction: Although COVID-19 is now considered an endemic disease, understanding the factors associated with planned extubation and self-extubation in this population remains essential. Objective: To identify factors associated with self-extubation, planned extubation and mortality in patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia. item.title: Gastric ultrasound to predict intolerance to enteral nutritional support: a prospective cohort
item.description: Introduction: Bedside-focused ultrasound has opened new avenues for monitoring critically ill patients. Measurement of the gastric antral area (GAA) and residual gastric volume (RGV) have been proposed as predictors of intolerance to enteral nutritional support (ENS). Objectives: To assess the diagnostic performance of GAA and RGV via ultrasound for predicting ENS intolerance. item.title: Prognostic factors of postoperative dissatisfaction: a cohort study
item.description: Introduction. Patient satisfaction is a priority due to its relationship with the quality of care provided. The incidence and prognostic factors associated with patient satisfaction are uncertain in the Colombian setting. Objective. To estimate whether sex, age, fasting hours, time scheduled for surgery, surgery cancellation, socioeconomic status, and length of stay are prognostic factors of patient dissatisfaction. Methods. item.title: Preoperative risk scales in pediatric anesthesia: a narrative review
item.description: Preoperative evaluation in pediatric patients is intended to identify risk factors that may be associated with perioperative complications. This assessment is often performed similarly to that of adults; however, children have specific considerations. Moreover, most scales designed for perioperative risk classification have not been validated in the pediatric population.
